tasks.summary: The scope-verification mechanism added to ExecutorProgressRelay (confirmScope / analysisProgressPath / pending-verified-rejected state machine) is correctly wired end to end (analyze-rpc.ts → executor-relay.ts → access.ts projectForScope) and is exercised by the "redirected" case in the S2 analysis test, which proves a classified scope that resolves to a different registered project is fenced to 'interrupted' without ever flushing the mismatched sample to the trusted producer. The admission/ambiguous-origin, early-terminal, quiet-owner-probe, workflow-streaming, and cached/aborted/failed analysis paths are each covered by a corresponding unit test, and the builder's focused run of that suite passed at this pin. However, the task's own functional summary states T5 (the live-daemon integration test `S2 real daemon routes concurrent workflow and analysis progress to isolated observers` in executor-qualification.test.ts) is unvalidated at this pin, and the full backend regression sweep remains red with a re-run still in progress. testCoverage.explanation: The unit-level executor-relay.test.ts suite (7 cases) adequately covers the acceptance checks for admission binding/ambiguity, stale/foreign/malformed event rejection, early-terminal preservation, quiet-owner probing with worker-loss fencing, and — critically — the new scope-confirmation state machine (the 'redirected' sub-case in the analysis test proves a post-classification scope mismatch is fenced to 'interrupted' rather than leaking data into the wrong project's progress channel). tasks.summary: t3 wires workflow.run / workflow.run.start execution owners to the shared progress relay. Verified the four changed files (handler-runtime.ts, workflow-rpc.ts, workflow-run-registry.ts) at the review pin 1d7f50452332b3a2d2e8e7a2c7207040e2891fe5 match the embedded diff exactly, cross-checked against the parent commit, and confirmed the call-site signatures (analyze-rpc.ts runStart, request-context.ts TrustedRpcContext.executorProgressPort, threads/router.ts port-transfer) that this task's wiring depends on. All three t3 acceptance checks from PLAN.md (byte-compatible streaming/detached frames; single observation per entry path; exactly-one settled status with observer-loss resilience) are satisfied by the code and exercised by the two integration tests named for t3 ("S2 workflow progress preserves streaming frames and terminal result", "S2 detached workflow preserves poll cursor and abort behavior across observer loss"), both reported passing by the builder at this exact pin.

testCoverage.explanation: Read the full executor-relay.test.ts at the review pin. The two tests named against t3 directly exercise both entry paths: 'S2 workflow progress preserves streaming frames and terminal result' asserts observed frames deepEqual the legacy (no-port) run, asserts the exact stream-type sequence ['progress','delta','progress','delta','done'] (confirming token batching/tail/byte-compatibility), and asserts the final stored measurement's stageId and production (output-chunks completed:17) match the 17 onToken calls plus two onProgress calls — directly covering the 'byte-compatible' and 'measured cumulative output' acceptance checks. 'S2 detached workflow preserves poll cursor and abort behavior across observer loss' drives startWorkflowRun with a stalled provider turn, disconnects the origin (observer loss), polls (frames/cursor preserved), aborts, and asserts settle('cancelled') fires exactly once with resultRef=runId — covering 'observer loss leaves detached work active' and 'exactly one settled status' for the cancel path. The 'nested grounding does not create separate observations' check is structurally guaranteed (beginWorkflowProgress is invoked exactly once per runStart/startWorkflowRun call and the resulting `observation` closure is shared by every onProgress/onToken callback for that call) rather than independently asserted, but the code construction makes a second observation impossible for a single call, which is consistent with how the LLD states the guarantee. Settle idempotency (ended flag in beginExecutorProgress) is exercised by the producer-relay tests (early-terminal / worker-loss cases) at the shared-primitive level, which workflow-rpc.ts and workflow-run-registry.ts consume unchanged.

tasks.summary: t4 wires analyze.run.start to the executor-progress observation seam (beginExecutorProgress/AnalysisMeasurements) at analyze-rpc.ts, and threads the new progressPort parameter through handler-runtime.ts's analyze.run.start dispatcher. All five selected blocks match the committed source at the pinned revision 1d7f50452332b3a2d2e8e7a2c7207040e2891fe5 exactly, and the current checkout's copies of both changed files and both test files are byte-identical to that pin. The wiring is minimal and correct: observation is created only when a MessagePort is supplied, confirmScope fires on the 'classified' event and again (idempotently, since beginExecutorProgress guards with scopeConfirmed) from result.intent for the cached/no-event path, measurements.onEvent gates which typed events produce a sample (preview/llm-token and nested/child-task events with parentTaskPath are excluded by AnalysisMeasurements' own filtering), and settle is called exactly once on every exit path: the invalid-params early return (before progressPort is touched, intentionally, since the LLD's sc2 contract says admission/observation must never block the legacy terminal path), the uncaught-throw catch block (settled 'failed'), and the normal completion path (settled 'completed'/'cancelled'/'failed' based on result.ok and the aborted error code).

testCoverage.explanation: The two named integration tests ('S2 analysis progress preserves stage frames and the analyze.result then done sequence', 'S2 analysis preserves cached completion cancellation and persisted status') exercise runStart (aliased runAnalysis) directly through a real ExecutorProgressRelay/ProgressCoordinator/ProgressStore fixture, not mocks of the changed seam. The first test drives a full classify/plan/execute event sequence through the real onEvent callback, asserts the legacy frame stream is byte-identical with and without progress wiring (so the new code cannot alter legacy behavior), asserts the persisted measurement snapshot matches AnalysisMeasurements' expected shape, confirms analysisProgressPath's symbol-vs-non-symbol behavior directly, and exercises the result.intent-driven confirmScope/redirect path which settles as 'interrupted' with a non-'execute' stageId (proving no progress is fabricated past the actual stage reached). The second test exercises: a fully cached completion (no events fired at all) settling 'completed' with a null measurement — proving the cached-result path uses the actual stored result rather than synthesizing progress; a pre-aborted run whose result.error.code is 'aborted' settling 'cancelled'; and an unhandled throw from the orchestrator settling 'failed' via the catch-block code path (line 634) while still emitting the terminal analyze.result/done frame pair. Together these two tests cover all three acceptance checks listed for t4 and match the actual changed line ranges (587, 621-628, 634, 673-674) rather than only the surrounding scaffolding. The invalid-params early-return path (which intentionally skips progress wiring per the LLD's sc2 contract) is not separately exercised by these two tests, but it is unchanged by this diff and is covered by the `mapper: malformed / unknown input -> null, never throws`-style tests in the broader suite; its behavior is also directly verifiable by code inspection (observation is simply never created, so no terminal/leak concern arises beyond the relay's existing 10s admission timeout, which is pre-existing S2 infrastructure out of this task's scope).

advice: Optional execution: I did not re-run the focused test command (node --import tsx --test ... executor-relay.test.ts analyze-progress.test.ts ...) myself — the shell tool in this review session required an approval step that wasn't available, so I relied on static inspection plus the builder-reported pass evidence. I did verify that the current checkout's src/daemon/analyze-rpc.ts, src/daemon/handler-runtime.ts, and both named test files are byte-identical (git diff --stat, no output) to the pinned commit 1d7f50452332b3a2d2e8e7a2c7207040e2891fe5, so the builder-reported focused run's source matches what is being reviewed here.

Optional improvement (nonblocking): the catch block at line 634 settles 'failed' before attempting to read/repair the run record for logging (lines 644-653); this is pre-existing code outside the diffed segments and not a defect, just noting it for completeness.
